title: Network shielding Terraform module for VPC egress, SGs, NACLs, and private DNS
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that codifies Redwood's VPC network defense posture for Private deployments. The module will manage layered controls: least-privilege security groups, subnet-level NACLs with explicit allow/deny egress rules, private DNS forwarding (Route53 Resolver endpoints), and configurable egress enforcement (proxy endpoint or forced-tunnel via NAT + proxy). It must support multi-account use, predictable upgrade paths for existing customers, and integrated health checks and drift detection hooks for operational visibility.
background: We currently lack a single, battle-tested IaC module that captures recommended security controls for Private/VPC deployments. Engineering teams repeatedly copy patterns across repos which leads to drift, inconsistent egress handling, and noisy support. This module will be the canonical artifact used by Redwood Private installations and as the default template for dedicated customer deployments.
technical_approach: Expose a minimal surface: create_security_groups=true, apply_nacls=true, dns_forwarding=true, egress_mode={deny-by-default|proxy|nat-only}
Security groups generated from a small set of role templates (control-plane, workload, monitoring) with tags to allow cross-account referencing and least-privilege CIDR inputs
NACL templates applied per-subnet with ordered rules and explicit ephemeral port allowances for managed services
Private DNS implemented via Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints or conditional forwarders when using on-prem DNS; module includes permissioned IAM role for resolver association

Egress enforcement supports three modes: 1) deny-by-default with explicit allowlist, 2) forced-tunnel through customer-managed proxy (requires proxy endpoint ARN), 3) NAT gateway enforcement for legacy workloads
Upgrade strategy: module versioning, migration helpers (scripted Terraform import plans + plan checks), and a non-destructive default to keep existing rules when possible

Health and observability: optional CloudWatch (or provider equivalent) alarm integration; a lightweight 'module-health' Lambda that runs periodic checks for Resolver health, NACL hit counts, SG flow logs, and surface findings via a SNS topic
Testing: unit tests with terratest, full-plan-run integration in CI against a disposable VPC, and negative tests for broken configs
Drift detection: integration with existing infra-sentry job to run periodic terraform plan and alert on diffs
Documentation: usage examples for single-account, multi-account (cross-account resolver associations), and on-prem bridged networks
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to internal registry with semver tags and a CHANGELOG
Module exports: security_group_ids, nacl_ids, resolver_endpoint_ids, egress_policy_description string
Module includes migration script and documented upgrade playbook for customers with pre-2025 handcrafted rules
Automated terratest suite passes in CI and a reproducible integration test that creates a disposable VPC and verifies DNS forwarding and enforced egress
Health Lambda and CloudWatch dashboards created as optional outputs; alerts fire in a smoke test when we intentionally break resolver association
Security review completed and artifacts stored in Confluence with an SRI checklist sign-off
Module has examples for proxy-based egress and deny-by-default configurations and at least one internal team adopts it for staging deployments

comments: Lina Gomez (Security): Please ensure the default egress allowlist is empty and that the change-log highlights breaking behavior if teams rely on implicit outbound access.
Marcus Li (Infra): Suggest exposing an output for the resolver IAM role ARN to make cross-account association automation simpler.
Jonas Meyer (Assignee): Will add migration helper that snapshots existing SGs and NACLs and produces a terraform import plan to reduce blast radius during upgrade.
PM review (Priya Shah): Need an example in docs showing how to opt into 'proxy' mode with an externally managed proxy endpoint and how billing/egress metering works.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Upgrading an existing customer's handcrafted rules may accidentally remove necessary egress paths. Mitigation: provide non-destructive migration scripts and an 'import-only' mode that annotates resources without changing them.

Risk: Cross-account resolver associations require tight IAM coordination. Mitigation: provide a clear runnable playbook and a small helper that generates the required IAM trust policy artifacts for reviewers.
Risk: Performance/latency when forcing traffic through a proxy. Mitigation: document trade-offs and recommend a staged rollout with canary subnets and metrics monitoring.
